item.title: Austin Regular Meeting: March 26, 2026
item.description:
Here's a summary of the Austin City Council agenda: * **Major Housing and Land Use Reforms:** Council will consider resolutions to allow more "missing middle" housing (like townhomes and small multi-unit buildings), encourage mixed-use developments, update rules for home-based businesses, and reduce or unbundle parking requirements in transit-friendly areas to boost housing options and local commerce. * **City Boundary Adjustments (Disannexations):** Multiple public hearings are scheduled to remove various properties from Austin's full-purpose jurisdiction, a direct response to state law (SB 1844) impacting many residents. * **Key Infrastructure & Transportation Planning:** Decisions include adopting a new Austin Core Transportation Plan, authorizing millions for climate pollution reduction initiatives, acquiring a new reuse warehouse for Austin Resource Recovery, and approving significant contracts for water and stormwater infrastructure projects. * **Homelessness & Public Health Strategy:** The Council will adopt its 2025-2027 Strategic Plan for addressing homelessness and approve continued funding for community-based opioid overdose prevention and recovery services.

item.title: Austin Austin Housing Finance Corporation: March 26, 2026
item.description:
Here are the key items from the Austin Housing Finance Corporation agenda: * The Austin Housing Finance Corporation will consider authorizing a **$3.5 million loan** to support the **Sunday Village** affordable housing project. * This funding is designated for National Church Residences (or an affiliated entity) for the property located near 1026 Clayton Lane. * The loan is intended as permanent debt for the project, drawing from the Corporation's Fiscal Year 2025-26 Capital Budget.

item.title: Austin Work Session: March 24, 2026
item.description:
Here's a summary of the Austin City Council agenda: * **Future of Homelessness Services:** Council will review a 2025-2027 strategic plan outlining future policies, investments, and partnerships to address homelessness in Austin. * **Housing & Zoning Reform:** Discuss significant changes to the Land Development Code to create new zoning districts, allowing for more "missing middle housing" (like townhomes and cottage courts) and "mixed-use" developments (combining residential and commercial uses). * **Public Sign Regulations:** Hold a public hearing on an ordinance that would allow larger, electronic, and off-premises advertising signs in the public right-of-way. * **I-35 Cap and Stitch Project:** Receive an informational briefing on the recommended designs for the Austin I-35 Cap and Stitch project, a major infrastructure initiative.

item.title: Austin Regular Meeting: March 12, 2026
item.description:
Here's a summary of the Austin City Council agenda in 3-5 bullet points: * **Massive Infrastructure Investment:** Council will consider approving over $1.5 billion in funding for the Walnut Creek Wastewater Treatment Plant expansion, including a potential $1 billion federal loan and a $600 million increase to an existing construction contract. * **Future of City Golf Courses:** A major policy discussion will initiate the rezoning process for the 445-acre Jimmy Clay and Roy Kizer Golf Courses, a significant land-use decision for these city-owned properties. * **City Lobbyist and Affordable Housing Policies:** The agenda includes proposed updates to city lobbyist regulations and an amendment to a development agreement at 800 E. St. John Avenue aimed at providing deeper affordable housing. * **Public Hearings on Zoning Changes:** Multiple public hearings are scheduled for proposed zoning and land use changes across the city, including significant mixed-use developments and increased residential density in several neighborhoods.

item.title: Austin Regular Meeting: February 26, 2026
item.description:
Here's a summary of the Austin City Council agenda: * **Major Airport Expansion Funding:** Council will vote on issuing approximately **$1.4 billion in bonds** to fund the ongoing expansion of Austin-Bergstrom International Airport (ABIA). * **Significant Homelessness Initiatives:** The agenda includes committing over **$50 million** for operating costs of emergency shelters (including future Esperanza II shelter) and expanding street outreach, as well as adopting the 2025-2027 Strategic Plan to address homelessness. * **City Boundary & Land Use Changes:** Public hearings will be held on numerous zoning amendments across the city, often changing land use from single-family or office to mixed-use and commercial, and officially **disannexing several properties** as required by state law (Senate Bill 1844). * **New City Oversight and Public Safety Policies:** Council will consider establishing a **Comprehensive Efficiency Assessment Program** for the City Auditor, creating a rubric to guide future social service contract funding decisions, and approving a new ordinance related to **vehicle engine noise**.

item.title: Austin Work Session: February 24, 2026
item.description:
Here's a summary of the Austin City Council agenda: * **New Vehicle Noise Ordinance:** Council will consider approving a new city ordinance to regulate vehicle engine noise, creating an offense for violations. * **Addressing Homelessness Strategy:** Members will receive a key briefing on the strategic plan for addressing homelessness in Austin for the upcoming fiscal year. * **Boosting Climate Action Funding:** A vote is scheduled to increase funding by $5 million for an EPA grant, strengthening the city's climate pollution reduction initiatives. * **Parks & Recreation Software:** Council will consider approving a $2 million contract for new software to improve how Austin's Parks and Recreation facilities and programs are managed.
